mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.00% in a given month reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected equity cash flows and thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.00% in the month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in the same month are not statistically different from a pre-tightening baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 5.00% in any subsequent month.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +2.0% in a month, it indicates accelerating inflation, prompting the Fed to maintain higher short-term rates and suppressing equity discount rates, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (t-test p < 0.05) despite ΔCPIAUCSL > +2.0%, or Fed cuts rates within 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS (labor market additions) of at least 50,000 jobs in the prior month is associated with stronger consumer demand and corporate hiring optimism, which elevates S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥ 50,000 in the prior month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically superior to a baseline of no job growth (t-test p > 0.05), or monthly job growth < 50,000 for the next 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both HOUST (industrial production) and RSAFS (retail sales) by at least 2% in the same month signals weakening demand across sectors, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < -2% AND RSAFS < -2% in the month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05), or either HOUST or RSAFS recovers ≥ 2% in the following month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly INDPRO index below 90.0 indicates contracting industrial production capacity utilization, which reduces future supply chain confidence and tends to depress S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in months with INDPRO < 90.0 are not negative (p > 0.05), or INDPRO crosses above 90.0 within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 5.0% for three consecutive months, it reflects weakening labor market conditions and a shift toward lower wage growth expectations, which tends to depress equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during the cooling period, or UNRATE rises above 5.0% within 4 months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in GDPC1 (real GDP momentum) of at least 3% over a quarter suggests economic softening that lowers growth expectations and compresses discount rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) despite GDPC1 decline, or GDP momentum recovers ≥ 3% in the following quarter.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both FEDFUNDS and HOUST (industrial production) create a dual contractionary signal: higher rates reduce discounting while weak production erodes demand expectations, jointly predicting negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < prev AND HOUST < prev in the month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) despite both proxies falling, or either proxy recovers in the following month.
